history.summary: IDENTITY UNCERTAIN — thin documentation. 'Bhawani Temple' is documented as one of the first shrines encountered on the Girnar hill trek, dedicated to Goddess Bhawani, and is believed by pilgrims to grant blessings for a prosperous life (cultureandheritage.org, 2025). No source gives its builder, date, or exact position; it should NOT be confused with the Bhavnath Mahadev Temple (a Shiva temple at the Girnar base in Bhavnath village) nor with the Ambika/Ambaji temple higher up the hill. Coordinates (21.5240, 70.5120) are APPROXIMATE: a point on the Girnar trek route near Junagadh, since no POI-level coordinates are published. Treat as a minor shrine on the pilgrimage path rather than a major documented temple.

name: Bhawani Temple
town_description: Junagadh is a historic city in Gujarat's Saurashtra region, nestled at the foot of Mount Girnar. Its past stretches from Ashoka's 3rd-century BCE rock edicts and the Uparkot Fort to the Nawabi-era Mahabat Maqbara, and it is a major pilgrimage hub for both Hindus and Jains.

travel.airport: Keshod (~40 km) or Rajkot (~103 km) from Junagadh
travel.railway: Junagadh Junction (~6 km from Girnar Taleti, the base)
travel.road: Girnar Taleti base reached by road from Junagadh; the shrine lies on the stepped trek route up Mount Girnar
